text: A US Army manual (1935, 1943) cuts a key phrase in two: the first part reorders the message alphabet, the second the carved alphabet, and the whole phrase is the repeating key.

Every pair of the puzzle's words and every short run of words from K1-K3, split at each word boundary: 29,880 phrases, three ways of numbering the key, three table rules, on K4 and ten scrambled copies.
The best phrase gives 7 of the 24 known letters, as on the copies (7-8). Closed.
